claim_1.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of heparinized whole blood from young adults (25–40 yo, n=15) and elderly adults (60–79 yo, n=21) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed significant CD4+ T cell responses after Zostavax® compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: In contrast significant CD4+ T cell responses were detected in the majority of subjects (Figure 1B), consistent with a recent report (Qi et al., 2016).

Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses B) CD8+ and CD4+ T cell activation as measured by Ki67+Bcl2- in young adults (black, n=13 for CD8+, n=15 for CD4+) and the elderly (orange, n=19 for CD8+, n=21 for CD4+). Mean values in solid lines, and shades for 90% confidence interval.

claim_2.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of cryopreserved PBMCs from young adults (25–40 yo, n=16) and elderly adults (60–79 yo, n=20) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed increased CD4+CXCR5+CXCR3+ICOS+ Tfh-like cells after Zostavax® in both age groups compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Figure 1C shows an increase in CD4+CXCR5+CXCR3+ICOS+ T cells after Zostavax® in both the young and elderly adults.
Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses C) Increase in VZV-specific Tfh-like cells (as measured by CXCR5+ICOS+CXCR3+) in young adults (n=16) and the elderly (n=20).

claim_3.claim: ELISPOT analysis of PBMCs from young adults (25–40 yo, n=17) and elderly adults (60–79 yo, n=22) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed increased antigen-specific IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-21 production by CD4+ T cells after Zostavax® compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Significant increase in CD4+ T cells that are positive for IFN-γ, IL-4 and IL-21 were also detected, indicating a mixed Th1/Th2/Th21 profile (Figure 1C).

Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses C) Increase in VZV-specific Tfh-like cells (as measured by CXCR5+ICOS+CXCR3+) in young adults (n=16) and the elderly (n=20). Antigen-specific IFN-γ, IL-4 or IL-21 production by CD4+ T cells as measured by ELISPOT in young adults (n=17) and the elderly (n=22). SFC = Spot forming cells.

claim_4.claim: ELISPOT analysis of PBMCs from vaccinated subjects after vaccination showed that depletion of CD4+ T cells, but not of CD8+ T cells, abolished IFN-γ production in response to vaccine peptides compared to undepleted cells.

sources.quote: Figure S1B shows that depletion of CD4+ T cells, but not of CD8+ T cells, abolished IFN-γ production in the ELISPOT assay.

claim_5.claim: ELISPOT analysis of PBMCs from a subset of HLA-A2+ individuals (n=13) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed no CD8+ T cell response to VZV HLA-A2-restricted vaccine peptides in most subjects after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Despite detectable VZV-specific CD8+ T cell responses at baseline, the CD8+ T cells did not respond to the vaccine peptides with the exception of two individuals (ZV113 and ZV118, Figure 1D).

Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses D) Antigen-specific CD8+ T cell responses and Zostavax DNAemia in a subset of HLA-A2+ individuals (n=13). PBMCs stimulated with previously published VZV-HLA-A2 restricted peptides overnight and IFN-γ measured via ELISPOT. Viral DNA copies in blood measured by PCR

claim_6.claim: PCR analysis of whole blood from vaccinated subjects at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed positive viral replication in the blood in only three subjects compared to the rest of the cohort.

sources.quote: Interestingly, when we examined VZV DNA in the blood, although residual amount of viral DNA was seen in some subjects at day 1 (Table S2), only three showed positive viral replication in the blood, including both the CD8+ responders (Figure 1D).

Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses D) Antigen-specific CD8+ T cell responses and Zostavax DNAemia in a subset of HLA-A2+ individuals (n=13). PBMCs stimulated with previously published VZV-HLA-A2 restricted peptides overnight and IFN-γ measured via ELISPOT. Viral DNA copies in blood measured by PCR

claim_7.claim: ELISPOT analysis of PBMCs from young adults (25–40 yo, n=5) and elderly adults (60–79 yo, n=8) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed a transient peak of Zostavax®-specific plasmablast cells 7 days after vaccination (day 7) compared to days 0, 14, 28, 90 and 180.

sources.quote: We detected a transient peak of antigen-specific plasmablast cells 7 days after Zostavax® administration (Figure 1E), consistent with the plasmablast responses observed to other vaccines such as influenza (Wrammert et al., 2008).
Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses E) Representative VZV-specific IgG ELISPOT. Number of Zostavax®-specific plasmablasts in young adults (n=5) and the elderly (n=8).

claim_8.claim: ELISPOT analysis of PBMCs from young adults (25–40 yo, n=5) and elderly adults (60–79 yo, n=8) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed higher magnitude of the Zostavax®-specific plasmablast response in the younger group compared to the elderly group.

sources.quote: The magnitude of this cellular response was higher in the younger group (Figure 1E), consistent with previous studies with influenza vaccine (Sasaki et al., 2011).
Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses E) Representative VZV-specific IgG ELISPOT. Number of Zostavax®-specific plasmablasts in young adults (n=5) and the elderly (n=8).

claim_9.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from young adults (25–40 yo, n=16) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed significant increases in VZV glycoprotein-specific IgG induced by Zostavax® compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: The measurement of VZV glycoprotein-specific IgG over the course of the study showed significant increases induced by Zostavax® in both the young and elderly adults (Figure 1E).

Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses E) Representative VZV-specific IgG ELISPOT. Number of Zostavax®-specific plasmablasts in young adults (n=5) and the elderly (n=8). Kinetic analysis of Zostavax® glycoprotein-specific IgG antibodies as measured by ELISA in young adults (n=16) and the elderly (n=21).

claim_10.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from elderly adults (60–79 yo, n=21) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed significant increases in VZV glycoprotein-specific IgG induced by Zostavax® compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: The measurement of VZV glycoprotein-specific IgG over the course of the study showed significant increases induced by Zostavax® in both the young and elderly adults (Figure 1E).

Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses E) Representative VZV-specific IgG ELISPOT. Number of Zostavax®-specific plasmablasts in young adults (n=5) and the elderly (n=8). Kinetic analysis of Zostavax® glycoprotein-specific IgG antibodies as measured by ELISA in young adults (n=16) and the elderly (n=21).

claim_11.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from young adults (25–40 yo, n=16) and elderly adults (60–79 yo, n=21) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed that VZV glycoprotein-specific IgG peaked between two and four weeks after vaccination (days 14 and 28) compared to days 0, 1, 3, 7, 90 and 180.

sources.quote: The IgG antibody peaked between two and four weeks after vaccination, and dropped by 180 days after vaccination.

Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses E) Representative VZV-specific IgG ELISPOT. Number of Zostavax®-specific plasmablasts in young adults (n=5) and the elderly (n=8). Kinetic analysis of Zostavax® glycoprotein-specific IgG antibodies as measured by ELISA in young adults (n=16) and the elderly (n=21).

claim_12.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from young adults (25–40 yo, n=16) and elderly adults (60–79 yo, n=21) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed that VZV glycoprotein-specific IgG dropped by 180 days after vaccination (day 180) compared to the two- to four-week peak (days 14 and 28).

sources.quote: The IgG antibody peaked between two and four weeks after vaccination, and dropped by 180 days after vaccination.

Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses E) Representative VZV-specific IgG ELISPOT. Number of Zostavax®-specific plasmablasts in young adults (n=5) and the elderly (n=8). Kinetic analysis of Zostavax® glycoprotein-specific IgG antibodies as measured by ELISA in young adults (n=16) and the elderly (n=21).

claim_13.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from young adults (25–40 yo, n=16) and elderly adults (60–79 yo, n=21) at days 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed greater increase of VZV-specific antibody after vaccination in the younger group compared to the elderly group.

sources.quote: Direct comparison between the two groups indicates that the younger group had a greater increase of VZV-specific antibody after vaccination (Figure 1E).

Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses E) Representative VZV-specific IgG ELISPOT. Number of Zostavax®-specific plasmablasts in young adults (n=5) and the elderly (n=8). Kinetic analysis of Zostavax® glycoprotein-specific IgG antibodies as measured by ELISA in young adults (n=16) and the elderly (n=21). Inverse correlation between VZV-specific IgG at baseline and day 28 response is shown for young (black), elderly (organge) and the total cohort (blue).

claim_14.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from young adults (25–40 yo, n=16), elderly adults (60–79 yo, n=21), and the total cohort at baseline (day 0) and day 28 post-vaccination showed that the increase of VZV-specific IgG after vaccination was inversely associated with baseline VZV-specific IgG.

sources.quote: The increase of VZV-specific IgG after vaccination showed an inverse correlation to the baseline IgG (Figure 1E).

Figure 1. Zostavax® study overview, cellular and antibody responses E) Representative VZV-specific IgG ELISPOT. Number of Zostavax®-specific plasmablasts in young adults (n=5) and the elderly (n=8). Kinetic analysis of Zostavax® glycoprotein-specific IgG antibodies as measured by ELISA in young adults (n=16) and the elderly (n=21). Inverse correlation between VZV-specific IgG at baseline and day 28 response is shown for young (black), elderly (organge) and the total cohort (blue).

claim_15.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees at day 1 and day 3 post-vaccination showed that interferon induced antiviral genes MX1 and IFI44L and the phosphoserine phosphatase PSPH were highly upregulated compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Besides the interferon induced antiviral genes, such as MX1 and IFI44L, a phosphoserine phosphatase, PSPH, was highly upregulated at day 1/0 and day 3/0 (Figure S2A).

claim_16.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees at day 7 post-vaccination showed that immunoglobulin genes, TNFRSF17, and MZB1 were highly upregulated compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: At day 7, immunoglobulin genes were highly upregulated, as well as TNFRSF17 and MZB1, two genes extensively reported for their roles in antibody production (Li et al., 2014; Nakaya et al., 2011; Querec et al., 2009) (Figure S2A).

claim_17.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees, using blood transcription modules, at day 7 post-vaccination showed a strong plasmablast signature compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: BTM analysis of the response to Zostavax® revealed signatures seen with several other vaccines, including the seasonal influenza vaccines and the meningococcal vaccine such as a strong plasmablast signature at day 7 (Figure S2B), consistent with the robust plasmablast response at this time point (Figure 1E).

claim_18.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees, using blood transcription modules, showed weaker induction of innate immunity modules related to antigen presentation, dendritic cells, cytosolic DNA sensing, RIG-I receptor signaling, and type I IFN responses after Zostavax® compared to YF-17D.

sources.quote: Surprisingly however, several BTMs related to innate immunity including those relating to antigen presentation, dendritic cells, antiviral innate immune sensing including cytosolic DNA sensing, RIG-I receptor signaling and type I IFN responses were weakly induced by Zostavax® relative to YF-17D, which is another live viral vector (Figure S2B).

claim_19.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from healthy donors stimulated in vitro with Zostavax® showed uptake of VZV glycoprotein by a substantial proportion of monocytes, myeloid DCs, and plasmacytoid DCs compared to unstimulated cells.

sources.quote: We could detect VZV glycoprotein in a substantial proportion of monocytes, myeloid DC (mDC) and plasmacytoid DC (pDC) by intracellular FACS staining, suggesting uptake of virus by these cells (Figure S3A).

claim_20.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from healthy donors stimulated in vitro with Zostavax® showed no activation of monocytes, myeloid DCs, or plasmacytoid DCs, as evidenced by failure to upregulate CD80, compared to unstimulated cells.

sources.quote: However, there did not appear to be activation of these cell types in response to stimulation of PBMCs with Zostavax®, as evidenced by the failure to upregulate CD80 (Figure S3A), or release of proinflammatory cytokines in the supernatants (Figure S3B).

claim_21.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from healthy donors stimulated in vitro with Zostavax® showed no induction of IFNα in plasmacytoid DCs or IL-6 in monocytes and myeloid DCs compared to unstimulated cells.

sources.quote: Intracellular FACS staining of cytokines in these cultures revealed that Zostavax® failed to induce IFNα in pDCs (Figure S3C) or IL-6 in monocytes or mDCs (Figure S3D).

claim_22.claim: Cytokine Bead Array analysis of cell-free culture supernatants from PBMCs stimulated in vitro with Zostavax® showed induction of the chemokines CXCL8, CCL2, CXCL9, and CXCL10 compared to unstimulated cells.

sources.quote: However, Zostavax® induced several chemokines, such as CXCL8, CCL2, CXCL9 and CXCL10 in PBMCs (Figure S3E).

claim_23.claim: High-resolution metabolomics analysis of plasma from vaccinees at days 0, 1, 3, 7 and 14 post-vaccination showed the largest numbers of differential metabolites at day 1 and day 14 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Compared to the baseline, both negative and positive ionization data indicated the largest numbers of differential metabolites at day 1 and day 14 (under negative ionization, 429 and 425 peaks at FDR < 0.1, respectively).

claim_24.claim: High-resolution metabolomics analysis of plasma from vaccinees at day 1 post-vaccination showed that day 1/0 significant metabolite peaks had little overlap with chemicals in the vaccine compared to vaccine-derived peaks.

sources.quote: Few overlap peaks were found between the day 1/0 significant metabolite peaks and chemicals in the vaccine (data not shown), indicating that the human metabolomic changes were not simply due to carryover from chemicals in the vaccine.

claim_25.claim: High-resolution metabolomics analysis of plasma from vaccinees at day 1 post-vaccination, using mummichog pathway analysis, showed enrichment of TCA cycle, glycolysis and gluconeogenesis, and propanoate metabolism compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: We used the mummichog software, a pathway tool designed for untargeted metabolomics data (Li et al., 2013), to evaluate the day 1/0 significant metabolic pathways shown in Figure 2C. Strikingly, TCA cycle (and overlapping glycolysis and gluconeogenesis) and propanoate metabolism was also identified in the day 3/0 transcriptomics data (Table S3).

Figure 2. Plasma metabolomics and association with PBMC transcriptomics after Zostavax® vaccination C) Significantly enriched pathways for Day 1 vs Day 0 (both negative and positive ionization), by the mummichog software (Li et al., 2013).

claim_26.claim: High-resolution metabolomics analysis of plasma from vaccinees at day 1 post-vaccination, using regression modeling, showed that NK signature and T cell modules were negatively associated with metabolites in purine metabolism and lysine metabolism.

sources.quote: At day 1 after vaccination, both NK signature and T cell modules were associated with a number of metabolites (Figure 2D). Based on their regression coefficients, these were negative association, and the corresponding pathways, including purine metabolism and lysine metabolism (Figure 2D), largely overlapping with the day 1/0 significant pathway in Figure 2C.

Figure 2. Plasma metabolomics and association with PBMC transcriptomics after Zostavax® vaccination D) Metabolome-wide association with transcriptomics. The “chromosome” bands on the circular edge are 346 BTM gene modules in fixed order. Towards the center of the circle are scatter plots of −log10 p-values of metabolites that are significantly associated with the respective gene module (p < 0.01).

claim_27.claim: High-resolution metabolomics analysis of plasma from vaccinees at day 3 post-vaccination, using regression modeling, showed that linoleate metabolism, methionine and cysteine metabolism, glycerophospholipid metabolism, and glycosphingolipid metabolism were most strongly associated with PBMC gene expression for the MHC-TLR7-TLR8 cluster, antigen presentation and myeloid, DC activation via NF-κB, and B cell signatures.

sources.quote: At day 3/0, strong association to transcriptomics was seen in many metabolic pathways, including linoleate metabolism, methionine and cysteine metabolism, glycerophospholipid metabolism, glycosphingolipid metabolism. (Figure 2D). They were most strongly associated with gene expression for MHC-TLR7-TLR8 cluster, antigen presentation and myeloid, DC activation via NF-κB, and with B cell signatures.

Figure 2. Plasma metabolomics and association with PBMC transcriptomics after Zostavax® vaccination D) Metabolome-wide association with transcriptomics. The “chromosome” bands on the circular edge are 346 BTM gene modules in fixed order. Towards the center of the circle are scatter plots of −log10 p-values of metabolites that are significantly associated with the respective gene module (p < 0.01).

claim_28.claim: High-resolution metabolomics analysis of plasma from vaccinees at day 7 post-vaccination, using regression modeling, showed no significant association with PBMC transcriptomics compared to baseline-linked changes at earlier timepoints.

sources.quote: By day 7/0, no significant association was observed between transcriptomics and metabolomics (Figure 2D).

Figure 2. Plasma metabolomics and association with PBMC transcriptomics after Zostavax® vaccination D) Metabolome-wide association with transcriptomics. The “chromosome” bands on the circular edge are 346 BTM gene modules in fixed order. Towards the center of the circle are scatter plots of −log10 p-values of metabolites that are significantly associated with the respective gene module (p < 0.01).

claim_29.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees at day 7 post-vaccination showed that the gene module for plasma cells and immunoglobulins was positively associated with antibody secreting cells measured by ELISPOT at day 7.

sources.quote: For example, in Figure S4B, the gene module for “plasma cells and immunoglobulins” was correlated with antibody secreting cells at day 7/0, and the “T cell activation and signaling” gene module was correlated with total CD3+ T cells at day 3/0.

claim_30.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees at day 3 post-vaccination showed that the T cell activation and signaling gene module was positively associated with total CD3+ T cells measured by flow cytometry at day 3.

sources.quote: For example, in Figure S4B, the gene module for “plasma cells and immunoglobulins” was correlated with antibody secreting cells at day 7/0, and the “T cell activation and signaling” gene module was correlated with total CD3+ T cells at day 3/0.

claim_31.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees at day 7 post-vaccination showed that the recruitment of neutrophils gene module was positively associated with neutrophil numbers measured by flow cytometry in whole blood at day 7.

sources.quote: Even though transcriptomics was measured on PBMCs, the gene module of “recruitment of neutrophils” did correlate with the number of neutrophils measured by flow cytometry in whole blood at day 7/0 (Figure S4B).

claim_32.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees showed that early gene expression for calcium signaling and steroid metabolism was positively associated with later CD4+ T cell activation measured by flow cytometry.

sources.quote: Across time points, early gene expression for calcium signaling and steroid metabolism is correlated with later CD4+ T cell activation (Figure S4C).

claim_33.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees at baseline (day 0) showed that transcriptional signatures of the KIR clusters were positively associated with frequencies of NK cells measured by flow cytometry at baseline.

sources.quote: For example at baseline, there was a correlation between transcriptional signatures of the KIR clusters and the frequencies of NK cells.

claim_34.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees at baseline (day 0) showed that transcriptional signatures of cytosolic DNA sensing, chemokines and inflammation were positively associated with nuclear receptor 4 family signatures and neutrophil numbers measured by flow cytometry, and negatively associated with day 1 myeloid and dendritic cell activation via NF-κB genes.

sources.quote: Furthermore, at baseline the transcriptional signatures of cytosolic DNA sensing, chemokines and inflammation were positively correlated with nuclear receptor 4 family, with the number of neutrophils, but negatively correlated with day 1/0 genes of myeloid and dendritic cells activation via NF-κb.

claim_35.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees at day 3 post-vaccination showed that B cell signature genes were positively associated with the number of day 7 CXCR3+ Tfh-like cells measured by flow cytometry.

sources.quote: In addition, day 3/0 B cell signature genes are correlated with the number of day 7/0 CXCR3+ Tfh like cells (Figure S4D).

claim_36.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of blood cell populations from vaccinees across baseline (day 0), days 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed that major cell populations were stable within each study subject compared to between-subject variation.

sources.quote: The data in Figure S4D also suggest that major cell populations were stable for each study subject, which was confirmed by plotting the correlations between time points (Figure S4E), consistent with previous findings (Tsang et al., 2014).

claim_37.claim: Luminex analysis of plasma cytokines from vaccinees across baseline (day 0), days 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed that the majority of cytokines exhibited high stability within each subject compared to between-subject variation.

sources.quote: The majority of cytokines and metabolite clusters also exhibited high stability within each subject, while gene modules showed a more mixed range (Figure S4E).

claim_38.claim: High-resolution metabolomics analysis of plasma from vaccinees across baseline (day 0), days 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination showed that the majority of metabolite clusters exhibited high stability within each subject compared to between-subject variation.

sources.quote: The majority of cytokines and metabolite clusters also exhibited high stability within each subject, while gene modules showed a more mixed range (Figure S4E).

claim_39.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from young adults (25–40 years) and elderly adults (60–79 years) at baseline (day 0) showed higher inflammation, cytosolic DNA sensing, and NK cell gene modules in the elderly group compared to the young group.

sources.quote: The most significant gene network consisted of gene modules related to inflammation, cytosolic DNA sensing and NK cells, which were significantly higher in the elderly group (Figure 4B), consistent with our recent results(Nakaya et al., 2015).

Figure 4. Age difference explained by MMRN A) The subnetwork from MMRN related to age groups, colored by t-score in comparison between the young and elderly groups. Red indicates higher value in elderly. The most significant gene network is shown in B) and C), cytokine network in D).

claim_40.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from young adults (25–40 years) and elderly adults (60–79 years) at baseline (day 0) showed lower IL7R expression in the elderly group compared to the young group.

sources.quote: Interestingly, there was lower expression level of IL7R gene in the elderly group (Figure 4C, by red arrow), suggesting a potential compensatory mechanism.

Figure 4. Age difference explained by MMRN A) The subnetwork from MMRN related to age groups, colored by t-score in comparison between the young and elderly groups. Red indicates higher value in elderly. The most significant gene network is shown in B) and C), cytokine network in D). In C), each column represents a subject at day 0, colored by z-scores of gene expression values. IL7R is marked by a red arrow.

claim_41.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young adults (25–40 years) and elderly adults (60–79 years) at baseline (day 0) showed higher NK cell frequencies in the elderly group compared to the young group.

sources.quote: Furthermore, difference in NK cells measured by flow cytometry (Figure 4E) was consistent with the transcriptomics data, and Luminex data supported the higher level of IL-7 in the elderly group (Figure 4F).
Figure 4. Age difference explained by MMRN E) Baseline NK cell frequencies measured by flow cytometry.

claim_42.claim: Luminex analysis of plasma from young adults (25–40 years) and elderly adults (60–79 years) at day 3 post-vaccination showed higher IL-7 levels in the elderly group compared to the young group.

sources.quote: Furthermore, difference in NK cells measured by flow cytometry (Figure 4E) was consistent with the transcriptomics data, and Luminex data supported the higher level of IL-7 in the elderly group (Figure 4F).
Figure 4. Age difference explained by MMRN F) Day 3/0 IL-7 levels measured by Luminex.

claim_43.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from females and males at day 3 post-vaccination showed higher activity of many T cell related gene modules in females compared to males.

sources.quote: In stark contrast to the age network, the sex related network shows the majority of activities that were higher in females at day 3/0 (Figure S6C), with many T cell related gene modules (Figure S6D).

claim_44.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from PCR+ and PCR− vaccinees showed higher baseline plasma cell signature genes, BCR signaling, heme biosynthesis, and inositol phosphate metabolism in the PCR+ group compared to the PCR− group.

sources.quote: The PCR+ group had higher baseline levels of plasma cells signature genes and BCR signaling, although these signatures were unlikely to have derived from VZV specific plasmablasts; they also had higher gene expression for heme biosynthesis and inositol phosphate metabolism (Figure S6E).

claim_45.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from PCR+ and PCR− vaccinees at day 7 post-vaccination showed higher cytoskeleton remodeling, cell adhesion, platelet activation, and G protein mediated calcium signaling in the PCR+ group compared to the PCR− group.

sources.quote: By day 7/0, the PCR+ group had higher activity in cytoskeleton remodeling (enriched for SRF targets), cell adhesion, platelet activation and G protein mediated calcium signaling (Figure S6E), possibly indicative of a response to viral replication.

claim_46.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from PCR+ and PCR− vaccinees at day 7 post-vaccination showed lower plasma cell signature genes in the PCR+ group compared to the PCR− group.

sources.quote: The PCR+ group also had lower activity in plasma cells signature genes at day 7/0 (Figure S6F), indicating a compromised antibody response.

claim_47.claim: Luminex analysis of plasma from PCR+ and PCR− vaccinees at day 7 post-vaccination showed higher RANTES in the PCR− group compared to the PCR+ group.

sources.quote: Interestingly, the day 7/0 cytokine RANTES is significantly higher in the PCR− group (Figure S6F).

claim_48.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees, using multivariate regression, showed that day 7 plasma cell, immunoglobulin, and B cell gene modules predicted the day 28/day 0 IgG response measured by ELISA.

sources.quote: These include the gene modules for plasma cells, immunoglobulin and B cells at day 7/0; a module on membrane and ER proteins at day 3/0, and small GTPase mediated signaling as a negative predictor at day 1/0.

claim_49.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees, using multivariate regression, showed that a day 3 membrane and ER proteins module predicted the day 28/day 0 IgG response measured by ELISA.

sources.quote: These include the gene modules for plasma cells, immunoglobulin and B cells at day 7/0; a module on membrane and ER proteins at day 3/0, and small GTPase mediated signaling as a negative predictor at day 1/0.

claim_50.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees, using multivariate regression, showed that day 1 small GTPase mediated signaling negatively predicted the day 28/day 0 IgG response measured by ELISA.

sources.quote: These include the gene modules for plasma cells, immunoglobulin and B cells at day 7/0; a module on membrane and ER proteins at day 3/0, and small GTPase mediated signaling as a negative predictor at day 1/0.

claim_51.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of blood cell populations from vaccinees, using multivariate regression, showed that day 7 IFN-γ+ T cells predicted the day 28/day 0 IgG response measured by ELISA.

sources.quote: Among the cell populations, day 7 IFN-γ+ T cells are the most significant predictor of IgG response (Figure S7B).

claim_52.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees showed that the day 1 and day 3 SREBF1 target network predicted Tfh-like cell response measured by flow cytometry.

sources.quote: The putative SREBF1 (sterol regulatory element binding transcription factor) target network at day 1/0 and day 3/0 was predictive of Tfh response, and the same network at day 7/0 was predictive of IgG response (Table S5, Figure 5A).

Figure 5. Predictors of adaptive immune response are redundant and dynamic A) The significant predictors of IgG (Figure S7B), IFNg+ T cells and Tfh like cells (Table S5) were identified using multivariate regression, then queried against the MMRN.

claim_53.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees showed that the day 7 SREBF1 target network predicted IgG response measured by ELISA.

sources.quote: The putative SREBF1 (sterol regulatory element binding transcription factor) target network at day 1/0 and day 3/0 was predictive of Tfh response, and the same network at day 7/0 was predictive of IgG response (Table S5, Figure 5A).

Figure 5. Predictors of adaptive immune response are redundant and dynamic A) The significant predictors of IgG (Figure S7B), IFNg+ T cells and Tfh like cells (Table S5) were identified using multivariate regression, then queried against the MMRN.

claim_54.claim: Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees at day 3 post-vaccination, using a regression model accounting for age, sex and study site, showed that SREBF1 target gene module M178 predicted the increase of Tfh-like cells measured by flow cytometry.

sources.quote: In this study, we found that day 3/0 SREBF1 targets was predictive of Tfh response (Figure 6A), and day 7/0 SREBF1 targets was predictive of antibody response (Figure 6B).
